title: Beyond Thirty: Treasury Issuance of Long-Term Bonds from 1953 to 1965

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: This staff report examines seven Treasury bonds with maturities beyond the conventional 30-year outer boundary that were issued between 1955 and 1963, including one 40-year bond. The paper analyzes the historical circumstances that led to the issuance of these longer-term instruments during a period before standardized 30-year issuance became the norm in the 1970s.
key_points: Seven bonds with maturities exceeding 30 years were issued between 1955 and 1963, including one 40-year bond
Thirty years has been the outer boundary of Treasury bond maturities since the emergence of regular issuance in the 1970s
The paper is authored by Kenneth D. Garbade and published as Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report Number 806
The paper is classified under JEL codes H63 (National Budget, Deficit, and Debt) and N22 (Financial Markets and Institutions: US, Canada)
The full paper is only available in PDF format, 36 pages
why_it_matters: This historical analysis provides context for understanding how Treasury issuance practices have evolved over time. While the findings are historical and not directly applicable to current market conditions, they illuminate how market structure considerations around duration and maturity selection have changed since the 1950s-60s.
market_structure_context: The source documents historical Treasury market structure evolution, specifically how the 30-year maturity boundary became established in the 1970s, providing historical perspective on Treasury market conventions
important_numbers: 7 bonds with maturities beyond 30 years issued between 1955-1963
30 years as outer boundary of Treasury maturities since 1970s
